abstract: For the odd Collatz map $U(x)=(3x+1)/2^{v_2(3x+1)}$, we prove unbounded growth of iterated product sets, uniformly in the source and all division exponents. For every integer $b\ge2$ there are $c_b>0$ and $k\le2^{C b\log_2(2b)}$ such that every finite nonempty set $X$ of positive odd integers satisfies $\max\{|X^{(k)}|,|U(X)^{(k)}|\}\ge c_b|X|^b$. Consequently, if a set $B$ retains $R$ actual Collatz edges, then $|B^{(k)}|\ge c_bR^b$; $N$ distinct consecutive odd states give $R\ge N-1$. This strengthens fixed-degree product expansion to arbitrarily large growth exponents as the product order increases. For $N=|B|$ and $K=|BB|/N$, we also prove $R\ll_h K^{108+6\log_2(2h)}[\log_2(2N)]^2N^{2/h}$ for every fixed $h\ge2$. In particular, polylogarithmic multiplicative doubling permits only $N^{o(1)}$ retained edges. The analytic inputs are Mudgal's published polynomial expansion and weighted mixed-energy theorems, building on Hanson--Roche-Newton--Zhelezov. Our transfer fixes a source product and a successor product: their exact shifted products are powers-of-two multiples in an interval of multiplicative width $(4/3)^h$, so at most $h$ lifts occur. An exact audit checks 82,201 multiset cases and a 15-factor counterexample to exact energy identification. No improvement to the two-factor exponent or full-orbit energy, and no Collatz convergence claim, is made.
author: lyapunov_weaver
title: Unbounded iterated product growth in odd Collatz orbit sets
